title: Tensors, Minibatches and Model Outputs
summary: Review separate tensor contracts, same-index minibatches and task-compatible layer dimensions.

steps.title: Construct PyTorch input tensors with compatible shapes and dtypes

blocks.text: For the numerical order arrays, feature and target representations have separate contracts. A shared feature dtype is not enough.

Import torch and construct each tensor with torch.from_numpy(array). Apply tensor.to(dtype=declared_dtype) separately to features and targets. Inspect shape and dtype, and verify corresponding observation order. Assert the declared axes and common batch length before returning the aligned tensors as a tuple.
Check the valid, boundary and failure fixtures with assert predicates. A false predicate raises AssertionError in ordinary, non-optimized execution.

blocks.code:
import torch

def aligned_pair(features_array, targets_array, feature_dtype, target_dtype,
                 feature_shape, target_shape):
    features = torch.from_numpy(features_array).to(dtype=feature_dtype)
    targets = torch.from_numpy(targets_array).to(dtype=target_dtype)
    assert features.shape == feature_shape
    assert targets.shape == target_shape
    assert features.dtype == feature_dtype
    assert targets.dtype == target_dtype
    assert features.shape[0] == targets.shape[0]
    return features, targets

import numpy as np
feature_dtype = torch.float32
target_dtype = torch.long

def inspect_pair(pair, feature_shape, target_shape):
    features, targets = pair
    inspected = (features.shape, features.dtype, targets.shape, targets.dtype)
    shape_ok = features.shape == feature_shape and targets.shape == target_shape
    dtype_ok = features.dtype == feature_dtype and targets.dtype == target_dtype
    alignment_ok = features.shape[0] == targets.shape[0]
    return inspected, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok

# Accepted fixture: four same-index observations.
features_array = np.arange(8).reshape(4, 2)
targets_array = np.arange(4)
accepted = aligned_pair(features_array, targets_array, feature_dtype,
                        target_dtype, (4, 2), (4,))
accepted_inspection, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok = inspect_pair(
    accepted, (4, 2), (4,))
assert shape_ok and dtype_ok and alignment_ok

# Declared illustrative boundary: one observation, two feature columns.
boundary_shapes = ((1, 2), (1,))
boundary = aligned_pair(features_array[:1], targets_array[:1], feature_dtype,
                        target_dtype, *boundary_shapes)
boundary_inspection, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok = inspect_pair(
    boundary, *boundary_shapes)
assert shape_ok and dtype_ok and alignment_ok

# Three-target failure: conversion succeeds; contract predicates fail.
short_targets_array = targets_array[:3]
converted_short = (torch.from_numpy(features_array).to(dtype=feature_dtype),
                   torch.from_numpy(short_targets_array).to(dtype=target_dtype))
short_inspection, shape_ok, dtype_ok, alignment_ok = inspect_pair(
    converted_short, (4, 2), (4,))
assert dtype_ok and not shape_ok and not alignment_ok
try:
    aligned_pair(features_array, short_targets_array, feature_dtype,
                 target_dtype, (4, 2), (4,))
except AssertionError:
    rejected = True
else:
    rejected = False
assert rejected

steps.title: Build a dataset and minibatch loader

blocks.text: The dataset defines a paired observation; the loader groups observations using a declared size and ordering policy.

In a map-style Dataset, __len__ supplies the sample count and __getitem__(index) supplies an item. For list observations, fetch features and targets at the same index and return a tuple. Configure DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=declared_size, shuffle=declared_order_policy), then iterate for features, targets in loader.

Batching preserves each item’s feature/target relationship. drop_last=True discards an incomplete final batch; drop_last=False, the default, retains it with fewer samples. Test boundaries against that policy. Use assert for valid, boundary and failure fixtures; false predicates raise AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

blocks.code:
from torch.utils.data import Dataset, DataLoader

class PairedItems(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, features, targets):
        self.features, self.targets = features, targets
        assert len(features) == len(targets)
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.features)
    def __getitem__(self, index):
        return self.features[index], self.targets[index]

features = list(range(5))
targets = list(range(5))
dataset = PairedItems(features, targets)
assert len(dataset) == 5
for index in range(5):
    assert dataset[index] == (features[index], targets[index])

# Retain the incomplete batch
retained_loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=2, shuffle=False, drop_last=False)
retained = list(retained_loader)
assert [len(x) for x, y in retained] == [2, 2, 1]
for x, y in retained:
    assert x.tolist() == y.tolist()
assert [i for x, y in retained for i in x.tolist()] == features

# Discard the incomplete batch
dropped_loader = DataLoader(dataset, batch_size=2, shuffle=False, drop_last=True)
dropped = list(dropped_loader)
assert [len(x) for x, y in dropped] == [2, 2]
for x, y in dropped:
    assert x.tolist() == y.tolist()
assert [i for x, y in dropped for i in x.tolist()] == features[:4]

steps.title: Five observations: retain or drop the last batch

blocks.text: In the supplied indexed-observation fixture, retaining the incomplete batch produces a smaller final batch; dropping it removes that batch. Neither policy creates observations. Verify __len__, item identities and batch boundaries. Same-index retrieval establishes pairing before collation: well-shaped batches can still contain mismatched items. Shuffle changes ordering, not the feature/target relationship, so do not assume the first loader item is the first source row.
A loader cannot fill a partial batch by assumption. Declare drop_last explicitly; establish alignment in each dataset item.

steps.title: Define a neural network with task-compatible layers and activations

blocks.text: Match layer widths and final outputs to the supplied task contract.

Import torch.nn as nn. An nn.Module subclass calls super().__init__(), registers layers as attributes and defines forward(self, x). nn.Linear(in_features, out_features) uses learned weights and bias to map feature vectors to outputs while preserving the leading minibatch dimension. nn.ReLU applies max(0, x) elementwise, introducing nonlinearity between linear layers.

nn.Sequential applies modules in declared order. Match each output width to the following input width. Choose final width and activation from the task contract, then verify output shape with a fixture batch.

blocks.text: Follow the supplied dimension chain for one observation, then restore the leading batch axis. Layer widths are per-observation dimensions, not sample counts. Let the supplied task determine final width and activation.
